subject: sociology
title: Labels in Schools and Streets
welcome_lead: From classroom 'troublemakers' to media 'folk devils', see labels in action in real studies.
meta_desc: GCSE Sociology adventure applying labelling theory to school, crime, mods and rockers.
final_note: Always pair a label with a study and an outcome — that nails AO2.

walkthroughs.body_html: Rosenthal and Jacobson (1968) told teachers some pupils were 'gifted' (when they were random). Months later those pupils improved more — proof of self-fulfilling prophecy.
Becker showed how labels become a master status. A teenager labelled 'criminal' may struggle to get jobs, mix with other labelled peers and drift into a deviant career — deviance amplification.
Stan Cohen's 1972 study of mods and rockers showed how media exaggerate a small clash into a moral panic. The group becomes a folk devil, more young people copy, and the cycle grows.

mcqs.q: What is a moral panic according to Cohen?
options: Disproportionate media reaction creating exaggerated public concern about a group or behaviour.
Genuine widespread fear about a real, serious threat.
Religious leaders condemning immorality.
The 'dark side' is a metaphor about families who don't communicate.

mcqs.q: What is a self-fulfilling prophecy in education?
options: A self-fulfilling prophecy is when teachers predict the future accurately.
Religious leaders condemning immorality.

When teachers' expectations (often based on labels) influence pupil behaviour and achievement — pupils labelled as 'bright' tend to do better, those labelled 'thick' worse, regardless of underlying ability (Rosenthal and Jacobson).
A self-fulfilling prophecy is when a student predicts their own grade correctly.

mcqs.q: What do feminists mean by the 'dark side' of family life?
options: The reality that families can be sites of inequality, exploitation and violence — particularly affecting women and children — challenging functionalist portrayals of the family as universally beneficial.
The 'dark side' is a metaphor about families who don't communicate.
A self-fulfilling prophecy is when teachers predict the future accurately.
The 'dark side' refers to families who live in poverty.
